scenarios.name: append-200
scenarios.description: 200 one-character appends by one writer, one transaction each: every event carries one character

scenarios.name: append-words
scenarios.description: appends of several characters each, merged into one block by the end

scenarios.name: insert-middle
scenarios.description: an insert inside an existing block splits it

scenarios.name: delete-range
scenarios.description: a delete inside one block

scenarios.name: delete-across-blocks
scenarios.description: a delete spanning a split block and an insert inside it

scenarios.name: insert-and-delete-in-one-transaction
scenarios.description: text inserted and partly deleted in the same transaction, garbage collection on

scenarios.name: insert-and-delete-in-one-transaction-no-gc
scenarios.description: the same with garbage collection off: the deleted text stays in the update

scenarios.name: delete-then-insert-at-same-place
scenarios.description: one transaction deletes a character and inserts another where it was

scenarios.name: delete-twice
scenarios.description: two deletes in one transaction, merged into one delete-set range per client

scenarios.name: format-plain-text
scenarios.description: formatting a range of plain text, then removing part of it, then appending

scenarios.name: embed
scenarios.description: an embed between appends

scenarios.name: text-insert-integer-attribute-keys
scenarios.description: insert with attribute keys that JavaScript enumerates as array indices

scenarios.name: text-insert-inherited-integer-key
scenarios.description: insert with one attribute where an integer-keyed attribute is in effect

scenarios.name: text-insert-empty-attrs-inside-run
scenarios.description: insert with an empty attribute object inside bold text

scenarios.name: text-insert-plain-at-run-end
scenarios.description: insert without attributes at the end of bold text

scenarios.name: text-insert-plain-at-run-start
scenarios.description: insert without attributes at the start of bold text

scenarios.name: text-insert-plain-after-deleted-run-end
scenarios.description: insert without attributes where the last bold character was deleted

scenarios.name: text-embed-attrs-inside-run
scenarios.description: insert an embed with another attribute inside bold text

scenarios.name: text-embed-plain-inside-run
scenarios.description: insert an embed without attributes inside bold text

scenarios.name: text-delta-cursor
scenarios.description: deltas whose ops continue from the cursor the previous op left

scenarios.name: text-delta-retain-past-end
scenarios.description: a delta formats past the end of the text

scenarios.name: text-insert-number-attr-from-peer
scenarios.description: insert with a number attribute equal to the one a peer wrote

scenarios.name: emoji-append
scenarios.description: an append after a surrogate pair; diffs include a state vector inside the pair

scenarios.name: map-overwrite
scenarios.description: a map key written three times and deleted

scenarios.name: map-keys-in-one-transaction
scenarios.description: several keys in one transaction, then one of them again

scenarios.name: array-push-merge
scenarios.description: pushes that merge into one block, then an insert and a delete inside it

scenarios.name: nested-map
scenarios.description: a nested map created, then written twice

scenarios.name: nested-text-in-array
scenarios.description: a text inside an array, appended to in separate transactions

scenarios.name: nested-type-deleted
scenarios.description: deleting a map that holds live keys: yjs deletes the keys too, so they are in the transaction's delete set

scenarios.name: nested-array-collected
scenarios.description: a deleted nested array becomes a garbage-collected run; diffs include state vectors inside the run

scenarios.name: empty-transaction
scenarios.description: a transaction with no edits, and one whose only edit changes nothing, emit no event

scenarios.name: origins
scenarios.description: the event carries the transaction's origin

scenarios.name: remote-apply
scenarios.description: a peer's edits applied with an origin; the receiver's event holds what it integrated

scenarios.name: remote-partly-known
scenarios.description: a peer's full state applied again after it grew: the receiver integrates only the new tail of a merged block

scenarios.name: concurrent-writers
scenarios.description: two writers editing the same text concurrently, synced both ways; diffs over both clients

scenarios.name: delete-set-is-the-transactions-own
scenarios.description: an append after a delete carries no delete set; a later delete carries only its own range

scenarios.name: remote-deleted-content
scenarios.description: a peer's full state carrying deleted content: the receiver's delete set holds that range

scenarios.name: remote-deleted-content-partly-known
scenarios.description: the receiver has the start of a block; the peer appends to it, deletes all of it and sends its state: the deleted struct is cut at the receiver's clock

scenarios.name: remote-collected-run-partly-known
scenarios.description: a peer's garbage-collected run whose start the receiver already has: the unknown tail must integrate

scenarios.name: remote-write-into-collected-parent
scenarios.description: a peer writes into a nested map another peer deleted concurrently: the write integrates as a collected run

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting
scenarios.description: two peers bold the same text concurrently; yjs follows the remote update with a cleanup transaction of its own

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-three
scenarios.description: three peers bold the same text concurrently; the receiving peers clean up after each remote update

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-different-keys
scenarios.description: one peer bolds, the other italicizes the same text concurrently: no key is duplicated, so the cleanup deletes nothing

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-inner-gap
scenarios.description: two peers bold the middle of xyz concurrently: the duplicates sit in an inner gap, which yjs's full cleanup does not reach

scenarios.name: remote-delete-formatted
scenarios.description: one peer bolds a while the other, not knowing it, deletes a: the receiving peer's contextless cleanup drops the opening marker, the other peer's full cleanup the closing one

scenarios.name: remote-unformat
scenarios.description: a remote update that only deletes format markers (an unitalic) calls for the full cleanup, which drops a leading bold:null an earlier contextless cleanup left

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-undo
scenarios.description: the cleanup after a remote update is a local transaction with origin null, so an UndoManager tracking null records it; undo and redo walk through it

scenarios.name: mixed-delete-content-first
scenarios.description: one remote update deletes content (higher client id) and a format marker (lower): yjs walks the content first, so its contextless cleanup runs before the deleted marker calls for the full cleanup

scenarios.name: mixed-delete-format-first
scenarios.description: the same with the clients swapped: the deleted format marker (higher client id) comes first and calls for the full cleanup, which takes the text out of the contextless cleanup of the deleted content

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-two-texts
scenarios.description: two texts bolded concurrently on both peers: one remote update, one cleanup transaction deleting a duplicate in each

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-untyped-root
scenarios.description: a third document only receives the concurrent formatting and never reads its root as text: yjs runs no cleanup for an untyped root

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-root-typed-late
scenarios.description: a document receives concurrent formatting while its root is untyped, then reads it as text: the text starts without formatting (yjs builds a fresh YText), so a remote delete runs no cleanup until a format marker arrives

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-xml-text
scenarios.description: two peers bold the same XmlText concurrently: a YXmlText is a YText, so the cleanup runs for it too

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-undo-grouped
scenarios.description: with grouping on, the cleanup merges into the step of the local bold before it: one undo takes both back

scenarios.name: concurrent-formatting-cleanup-clears-redo
scenarios.description: a cleanup after an undo is a captured change: it clears the redo stack

scenarios.name: cleanup-reaches-untyped-root
scenarios.description: a remote update changes a typed text, so the cleanup runs; its delete-set walk also cleans an untyped root of the same document, whose placeholder has _hasFormatting (doc 1 types its text first: a root typed after formatted text arrived inserts differently, docs/tech-debt.md)

scenarios.name: insert-into-root-typed-after-formatting
scenarios.description: a document receives bold text while its root is untyped, then types it and appends: yjs's fresh YText has search markers on (format markers turn them off only as they integrate), so the insert starts at a marker with no attributes and steps over the closing bold:null; ygo keeps walking from the start, collects bold and inserts before it (pinned, docs/tech-debt.md)

scenarios.name: cleanup-walks-deletions-in-order
scenarios.description: content that arrives deleted (the lower client's q, next to an inner gap holding two bold markers) is deleted while the update's structs integrate, before the delete set deletes the higher client's italic markers: yjs walks q first, and its contextless cleanup drops the duplicate, which walking by client id would skip

scenarios.name: cleanup-deletions-from-dependent-blocks
scenarios.description: an update relayed by a document that never reads the text (doc 4) brings doc 0 three clients' structs, all arriving deleted: the highest client's w was typed after the lowest client's q, next to an inner gap where doc 0 holds two bold markers (the writers of q and w saw one, so their own deletes cleaned nothing), and the middle client deleted a character of another root and its italic markers. yjs integrates w first, following its dependency into q, so q is the first deletion and its contextless cleanup drops the duplicate; ygo integrates in passes, the middle client first, whose italic markers put the text in the full cleanup, which does not reach the inner gap (pinned, docs/tech-debt.md)

scenarios.name: stack-chain-sets-keys-in-dependency-order
scenarios.description: one relayed update holds a key set by three clients in turn: the highest client's write follows the middle one's, which follows the lowest's, and each also sets a key of its own. yjs integrates the chain first (L's k, M's k, H's k), then H's h, M's m and L's l, so deleting the map and undoing it restores k, h, m, l; integrating in passes set k, l, m, h

scenarios.name: stack-takes-the-next-block-of-the-client-waited-on
scenarios.description: the highest client's key waits on the lowest client's fourth block, whose first three went into three other roots; yjs takes L's blocks one by one, the next each time, until the one waited on integrates: the types change in the order x, y, z, the map, h, then the middle client's root. Passes changed the middle client's root first

scenarios.name: stack-wall-then-retry
scenarios.description: doc 0 gets the highest client's two blocks without the lowest client's, which the first is typed after: both wait (the second has nothing to wait on but comes after the first), and when L's blocks arrive the retry integrates them in the same transaction

scenarios.name: stack-retry-waits-for-the-recorded-clock
scenarios.description: doc 0 gets H's X, typed after L's c (L:2), together with L's sixth block only (L:5): following X into L meets the hole before L:5, both wait, and yjs records L as missing from clock 4. L's first three blocks then arrive: L's clock is 3, not past 4, so yjs does not retry and X still waits, although what it was typed after is there now; retrying whenever something was queued integrated it here. L's next blocks pass clock 4, and the retry integrates X

scenarios.name: pending-real-block-after-a-skip
scenarios.description: a merged update carries L's first block (waiting on H) and fourth, with a Skip over the two between; then the real second and third blocks come, then H. The queue keeps no Skip, so the real blocks are not shadowed by it, and H's arrival lets all four of L's in

scenarios.name: fully-known-block-still-walls
scenarios.description: doc 0 knows H:0 only as a GC run, then gets H's own state, never collected: H:0 live with its parent in L, absent here, and an independent H:1. yjs checks a wholly known block's references too: H:0 waits on L and walls H, so H:1 waits as well, until L's state arrives and the retry lets it in

scenarios.name: partly-known-block-waits-on-its-original-reference
scenarios.description: client 30 is known up to clock 1 as a GC run; then a live 30:0..1 arrives whose origin, client 20's, is absent. yjs checks the reference as the block came, before cutting the known 30:0, so the block waits and 30 stays at 1; cutting first would re-point the origin at 30:0 and let 30:1 in

scenarios.name: deleted-runs-merge-without-gc
scenarios.description: with garbage collection off, adjacent deleted pieces of one block merge back into one struct

scenarios.name: replayed-delete
scenarios.description: an old update deleting part of a block, delivered again after the rest was deleted: nothing changes

scenarios.name: undo-grouped-deletes
scenarios.description: text written before the UndoManager, deleted one character per transaction in one undo step, then undone

scenarios.name: undo-nested-map-delete
scenarios.description: a nested map with keys deleted, undone (it comes back with its keys), redone, undone again

scenarios.name: undo-nested-array-delete
scenarios.description: a nested array of two blocks deleted and undone

scenarios.name: undo-nested-formatted-text-delete
scenarios.description: a nested text with a bold run deleted and undone: the format markers come back too

scenarios.name: undo-three-levels-delete
scenarios.description: a map in a map in a map, holding a text, deleted from the top and undone

scenarios.name: undo-types-in-array-delete
scenarios.description: a map and a text inside an array deleted together and undone

scenarios.name: undo-keeps-ancestors
scenarios.description: a tracked delete inside a map keeps the map: an untracked delete of the map then leaves its content uncollected

scenarios.name: undo-child-scope-parent-deleted
scenarios.description: a manager scoped to a nested map ignores the map's deletion, even though deleting it deletes a live key inside: its redo history survives

scenarios.name: undo-scope-recheck-two-managers
scenarios.description: a child-scoped manager does not delete what another manager restored into a new copy of the child

scenarios.name: undo-into-deleted-restored-parent
scenarios.description: undo restores a key into a parent whose restored copy was deleted again: the step counts, the earlier one stays

scenarios.name: undo-group-restore-before-delete
scenarios.description: one undo step inserted a map and deleted a key an untracked edit put in it: yjs restores the key, then deletes the map

scenarios.name: undo-clear-releases-keep
scenarios.description: after clear, a map the manager kept is released: an untracked delete of it is collected

scenarios.name: undo-fresh-edit-releases-keep
scenarios.description: undoing an insertion keeps what it deleted for redo; a fresh edit drops the redo step and releases the keep, so an untracked delete of the parent is collected

scenarios.name: undo-restore-order-concurrent-write
scenarios.description: one step deletes a key written by a middle client and the map holding it, with a lower client's write of the same key in between: yjs restores the lower client's value, because it walks deleting clients in deletion order

scenarios.name: undo-release-before-keep
scenarios.description: a fresh edit drops a redo step that kept the map it then deletes: the release comes first, so the map stays kept and undo restores it with its key

scenarios.name: undo-ends-capture-group
scenarios.description: an edit right after an undo opens a new step: the next undo removes only it

scenarios.name: undo-nested-multi-client
scenarios.description: a map created by a higher client ID holding keys from a lower one, deleted and undone by the lower: the parent is restored first

scenarios.name: undo-xml-element-delete
scenarios.description: an XML element with an attribute and a text child deleted and undone

scenarios.name: undo-clear-then-tracked-delete
scenarios.description: clear releases what a dropped step kept, including the parent, before the next step keeps it again: the parent's deletion after clear is undone with its remaining key

scenarios.name: undo-clear-other-manager-keeps
scenarios.description: one manager's clear does not take away a keep another manager adds after it: the second manager still restores the shared parent

scenarios.name: undo-clear-then-other-manager-undo
scenarios.description: one manager's clear, then another manager's undo restoring into the parent both kept: yjs releases at clear, before the undo keeps the parent again, so an untracked delete of the parent leaves its content

scenarios.name: undo-tracked-remote-delete-order
scenarios.description: a tracked remote update deletes keys of two clients: yjs applies its delete set in the order written, highest client first, so undo walks the clients in that order and leaves a concurrent write in place

scenarios.name: undo-out-of-scope-deletion-first
scenarios.description: one tracked transaction deletes a key outside the manager's scope, then one inside: yjs keeps the whole transaction's client order, so undo walks the outside key's client first and restores the inside key over a concurrent write

scenarios.name: undo-tracked-remote-blocks-before-deletes
scenarios.description: a tracked remote update whose higher client's write depends on a lower client's write in the same update: yjs integrates every block, both overwrites included, before the delete set, so the lower client's first deletion is an overwrite and undo walks that client before the delete set's others (GC off, so the overwritten write arrives with its content, not as a deleted struct)

scenarios.name: undo-tracked-remote-insertions-order
scenarios.description: a tracked remote update inserts keys of two clients into an empty document: yjs records insertion clients in the order they joined the store and deletes in reverse on undo, which decides the order redo restores them in

scenarios.name: undo-insertions-order-across-scope
scenarios.description: a tracked remote update inserts outside the manager's scope for a higher client and inside it for a lower one, then a grouped update inserts inside it for the higher: yjs keeps the insertion clients of the whole transaction in store order, so undo deletes the lower client's key last and redo restores it first

scenarios.name: undo-redone-copy-collected
scenarios.description: a deletion whose restored copy was later collected: yjs still counts undoing it as a change, so one undo does not go on to undo the step before

scenarios.name: undo-fresh-update-before-pending
scenarios.description: an update arrives while a block of one of its clients waits in the pending queue for it: yjs integrates the update's own blocks first and retries the queue after, so a key the update sets comes before the queued one in _map, and undo, walking keys in that order, leaves a concurrent write in place

scenarios.name: undo-nested-keys-in-arrival-order
scenarios.description: a map holding keys from two other clients, z arriving before a: deleting the map deletes them in the order they were first set, as yjs walks _map, so undo restores z first

scenarios.name: undo-nested-keys-from-one-update
scenarios.description: a map whose keys from two clients arrive in one update: yjs integrates the higher client first, so its key comes first in _map and is restored first

scenarios.name: undo-keys-from-dependent-blocks
scenarios.description: one update holds keys of three clients in a map: the highest client's key overwrites the lowest's, and a middle client's key is independent. yjs integrates the highest client's key first, following its dependency into just the lowest client's first key, then the middle client's, then the rest, so the keys first set come in that order and undo of the map's deletion restores in it

scenarios.name: undo-map-clear-order
scenarios.description: a map with keys from two clients, z set before a, cleared in a tracked transaction: yjs clears in _map order, and undo restores in that order

scenarios.name: undo-insertion-merged-into-restored-copy
scenarios.description: text typed right after a restored copy merges with it in yjs, kept or not, so undoing the original insertion deletes the typed text with it

scenarios.name: undo-deletes-merged-restored-copy
scenarios.description: a restore brings back an insertion and text typed after it as one struct in yjs; undoing the insertion through the other manager deletes the whole merged copy

scenarios.name: undo-array-restored-copy-merge
scenarios.description: an array element restored by undo merges with an element pushed right after it, as yjs merges kept items, so undoing the push deletes both

scenarios.name: undo-copy-then-collected-overwrite
scenarios.description: an untracked overwrite of a key whose value undo restored: yjs collects the overwritten value before merging, so it does not merge into the kept restored copy and goes out without content

scenarios.name: undo-copy-then-collected-array-neighbour
scenarios.description: an array element restored by undo, then one untracked transaction inserts after it and deletes both: yjs collects the new element before merging, so it does not merge into the kept restored copy

scenarios.name: undo-split-tombstone-restored-once
scenarios.description: a no-op undo cuts a merged kept tombstone, and yjs merges the pieces back at the end of that transaction, so a later undo restores it as one copy and a concurrent insert lands where yjs puts it

scenarios.name: undo-clear-merged-keep-parent
scenarios.description: clearing one manager releases exactly its own deletions inside a tombstone merged with another manager's: the other part stays kept, and its later release still walks up to the parent, so an untracked delete of the parent collects the subtree as in yjs

scenarios.name: array-push-after-trailing-tombstone
scenarios.description: push goes after the last struct, a trailing tombstone included (yjs typeListPushGenerics), so undoing the deletion of the last element brings it back before the pushed one

scenarios.name: array-insert-at-marker-boundary
scenarios.description: an insert by index where a search marker sits goes right after the previous live element, ahead of the tombstones before the marker, as yjs steps to n.prev

scenarios.name: array-insert-after-undo
scenarios.description: an undo deletes an array element before the one a search marker sits on; the next insert by index lands where yjs puts it (yjs popStackItem resets the markers)

scenarios.name: array-insert-after-remote-delete
scenarios.description: a remote delete removes an array element before the one a search marker sits on; the next local insert by index lands where yjs puts it (yjs resets the markers of a remote transaction)

scenarios.name: undo-redo
scenarios.description: UndoManager transactions emit updates with the manager as origin
